skill.name: literature-review
skill.description: Conduct systematic literature reviews across academic databases, verify citations, synthesize evidence, and generate markdown or PDF review documents.
skill.summary: Create systematic literature reviews with search guidance, citation checks, and formatted outputs.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in Markdown are false positives from code fences, inline command names, or reference URLs. Real risks remain in the workflow: broad Bash and write permissions, helper scripts that write files, DOI verification network calls, package-manager instructions, and Pandoc/XeLaTeX execution on user-supplied documents.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools where possible, and require explicit user confirmation before running shell commands or editing files outside the review workspace.
Validate input and output paths before running Pandoc, avoid arbitrary templates by default, and warn before processing untrusted markdown or bibliography files.
Resolve output paths under a dedicated output directory and reject absolute paths or parent directory traversal.

remediation.issue: External network calls for citation checks and database searches
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that DOI values and search terms may be sent to DOI.org, CrossRef, PubMed, bioRxiv, and other literature services.
Replace automatic install guidance with manual prerequisite documentation, or require user confirmation before pip, brew, or apt-get commands.

content.value_statement: Literature reviews require careful search design, citation checking, and reproducible documentation. This skill guides the full review workflow and provides scripts for formatting, deduplication, and citation verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides research question framing, scope definition, inclusion criteria, and database selection.
Documents search strategies for PubMed, bioRxiv, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, and biomedical databases.
Processes exported search results with deduplication, ranking, year filtering, and markdown or BibTeX output.
Verifies DOI metadata through DOI.org and CrossRef, then formats citations in common academic styles.
Uses a bundled review template to structure methods, results, discussion, limitations, and references.
Converts markdown review documents to PDF through Pandoc when local dependencies are available.
limitations: It does not replace expert screening, domain review, or final methodological judgment.
Database access depends on external services, APIs, installed tools, and any required credentials.
PDF generation requires Pandoc and XeLaTeX installed on the local system.
Citation verification sends DOI values to external services and may expose sensitive draft references.

use_cases.title: Plan a Systematic Review
use_cases.description: Define a research question, eligibility criteria, database list, and reproducible search protocol.

use_cases.title: Synthesize Technical Evidence
use_cases.description: Aggregate exported search results, remove duplicates, rank papers, and organize findings by theme.

use_cases.title: Prepare Publication Drafts
use_cases.description: Verify DOI metadata, format references, and generate a polished markdown or PDF review document.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Review Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a systematic literature review on [topic]. Define the research question, scope, databases, and inclusion criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Create Search Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Build database-specific search strings for [topic]. Include synonyms, Boolean logic, date limits, and expected sources for each database.

prompt_templates.title: Screen and Synthesize Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my exported search results to design a screening workflow, deduplication plan, quality assessment approach, and thematic synthesis outline.

prompt_templates.title: Finalize Review Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this literature review draft for citation accuracy, PRISMA completeness, limitations, synthesis quality, and PDF-ready structure.

output_examples.input: Plan a review about CRISPR therapies for sickle cell disease from 2015 to 2026.
output_examples.output: A structured protocol with a PICO question, PubMed and preprint search terms, inclusion criteria, screening stages, and quality assessment notes.

output_examples.input: Process exported article results and identify the strongest studies for a review.
output: A deduplicated search summary grouped by database and year.
A ranked paper list with titles, authors, sources, DOI links, and citation counts.
A thematic outline for the results section.

output_examples.input: Prepare a final review draft with verified citations and a PDF.
output_examples.output: A formatted review document with verified DOI metadata, consistent citation style, a references section, and PDF generation guidance.

best_practices: Document every database, search string, search date, filter, and result count before screening.
Use at least three complementary databases and record reasons for excluding studies.
Verify all DOI metadata and review external-service privacy implications before final delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one database search as comprehensive evidence coverage.
Do not summarize each paper separately when a thematic synthesis is required.
Do not run package managers, Pandoc, or citation scripts on untrusted files without user approval.

faq.question: Can this skill write a full literature review?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide structure, synthesis, citations, and formatting, but a domain expert should review the final argument.

faq.question: Does it search databases directly?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and scripts, and it can use compatible tools or APIs when they are installed and authorized.

faq.question: Which citation styles are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers APA, Nature, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE, with helper scripts for DOI-based citation formatting.

faq.question: Does citation verification require the internet?
faq.answer: Yes. The verification script uses DOI.org and CrossRef, so it needs network access and sends DOI values externally.

faq.question: Can it generate a PDF?
faq.answer: Yes, if Pandoc and XeLaTeX are installed. The bundled script converts markdown drafts into formatted PDF documents.

faq.question: Is it suitable for medical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It supports research synthesis, but it is not medical advice and should not replace professional judgment.
